topics.topic: Whether backup snapshots exclude agent-session records
questions: Are the new statements about holding the snapshot subject to the existing exclusion of agent-session records, or must a backup now retain every record visible in the snapshot?
Is “whatever the store holds” subject to the explicit exclusion of agent sessions, or must a later backup include an agent session present at its snapshot?

quotes:
A backup holds every record but the agent sessions (M06), which are
removed from the copy before it is encrypted, so the copy is a store of
its own that passes the same checks; Registry's other invariants are not
checked again in it, its transactions having kept them: a store restored
from it has no session, Kernel registers its sessions again and the owner
grants them again, so a restore never brings back a grant revoked after
the backup.

For a backup (A18 rules 1, 2): one consistent read snapshot of the whole store,
written as a store file of its own at the temporary path `backups` names and
makes for it, with the agent
sessions removed from that copy, so it passes the same checks; and the full
integrity and version check of such a file, the decrypted copy included,
opened for reading only.
judgement.why: The explicit agent-session exclusion qualifies the general snapshot wording, and State 3 assigns `store` ownership of producing that filtered snapshot copy.
